comment: Measured 2026-10-06 20:05: with TCP segmentation offload on, WSL hands Hyper-V 62 KB segments; uploads
from WSL then stalled the MediaTek MT7922 Wi-Fi transmit path within 2 s (router ARP probe failed,
~30 s outage). Windows own uploads: 0 loss. WSL uploads with TSO/GSO off: 0/72 lost.
This is what Codex (app-server in WSL) and Tailscale-in-WSL were triggering. eth0 is shared VM-wide.

The canonical MetroPlat name has an owned loopback hosts block for local offline use. WSL must preserve it at ordinary startup. Leader requirement 2026-10-26; no networking-mode change or WSL restart.
WSL interop (hv_sock) opens each Windows<->Linux channel with a vmbus ring that needs an
order-7 (512 KiB) physically contiguous allocation. Under agent load the VM fragments
until none exist, every wsl.exe/interop call hangs in UtilAcceptVsock, and Windows apps that
spawn into WSL (Codex Desktop) fail to start. Keep free headroom and compact proactively.
2026-10-06: WSL streamed a 113 GB core dump of a crashed Electron app onto C:, filling it; the VM then panicked.
Write no core dumps: a plain pattern honours RLIMIT_CORE, which is 0.
2026-10-18: with swappiness 10 and swap held to 256M, a cgroup at memory.high could reclaim only file pages,
which were the agents' own executables and databases: 12.4 GiB of refaults a minute. Swap now goes first to
the in-memory zram device (linux.zramSwap, priority 100), not the hv_storvsc disk, so anonymous and file pages
are weighed equally; the disk swap is overflow only.

headroomGuard.description: Compact memory on demand so WSL's hv_sock rings always find an order-7 block
comment: Measured 2026-10-09 11:30-11:36 CDT: with the VM at 6 GB, agents at their 4 GB ceiling and the node
at 1.5 GB, hvs_probe failed 'page allocation failure: order:7' (vmbus_alloc_ring) seven times,
UtilAcceptVsock timed out, and Windows powered the VM off at 11:36:39. min_free_kbytes and
compaction_proactiveness were set and did not prevent it. Each new channel needs one order-7 block;
32 keeps 16 MB of contiguous memory for a burst of launches.
cacheComment: WSL-20, 2026-10-14: under CI the VM's page cache grew to 6.2 GiB and held the VM at 9.95 GB with Windows
at 98% commit; gradual reclaim never fired because CI keeps the VM busy. One drop returned 4.4 GB to
Windows in 20 s. 3 GiB keeps the hot set; re-reads are served from Windows' own cache of the VHDX.
reclaimComment: WSL-22, 2026-10-18: Cached sat at 2.3-2.9 GiB, 1.9 GiB of it in Claude Code's batch commands (agent.slice);
a VM-wide drop would evict the interactive programs' executables with it. Take the excess from the batch
slices first, then the other services, and from the interactive cgroup last, through memory.reclaim.

comment: WSL boots with swiotlb=force: every Hyper-V storage transfer bounces through the swiotlb pool
(64 MB by default). A queue of 1267 requests x 252 KB per disk outruns it ~5:1 under load and the
VM dies with "hv_storvsc ... swiotlb buffer is full" (2026-10-05, three crashes). Size the queue to
the pool: 64 KB requests (<= 32 contiguous slots) and 256 in flight per disk = 16 MB.
2026-10-18: the kernel sized sdd's read-ahead at 8 MiB from the VHDX's reported optimal I/O size; under
memory pressure each refault of a mapped executable or database page reads around it by that window.

memory and 1.54 GB of page cache; 3G reclaims the cache, which is the churn that fragments
the VM, and leaves the processes room. Past HIGH the kernel reclaims page cache and throttles;
past MAX it OOM-kills the largest process inside this group only, never the laptop. Swap is a

while the VM held 7.05 of 8 GB, because the Guix release builds, the CI runner and the node ran in

Current 12G VM: agents 4G + user services 3.5G + Guix builds 1.5G + zram pool 1G = 10G, leaving 2G kernel headroom

relayReaper.description: Reap orphaned WSL relays before their vsock rings exhaust contiguous memory

zramSwap.description: In-memory compressed swap for idle anonymous memory, above the disk swap
comment: WSL-21, 2026-10-18: idle editor and app-server heap had nowhere to go but the 256M disk swap allowance, so
memory.high evicted executables instead. The WSL 6.18 kernel builds zram with LZO only (lzo-rle default).
2G of uncompressed swap in a pool bounded at 1G of RAM; the disk swap (/dev/sdc, priority -2) is overflow.

trimTimer.description: Return blocks freed in Linux to the Windows backing disk (fstrim on /)
comment: Group rule host-storage-reclaims-itself, Leader 2026-10-25 22:00 CDT: the VHDX held 580 GB on Windows for 436 GB of ext4
and no fstrim timer existed (systemctl list-timers showed none). A sparse VHDX gives back only the blocks Linux discards,
so the trim runs a few minutes after every boot (a restarted VM has forgotten which block groups it trimmed) and daily
after that, at idle I/O and CPU priority. One manual fstrim of / on 2026-10-25 trimmed 517.9 GiB.
